name: Bribery of Foreign Public Officials
description: Payments or benefits offered to foreign public officials to obtain or retain business or an improper advantage, typically disguised as consultancy, marketing, or commission payments routed through third parties or offshore entities. Financial institutions see the flows as unusual payments to or from intermediaries, officials' relatives, or shell companies.

sources.text: FATF, Specific Risk Factors in the Laundering of Proceeds of Corruption: Assistance to Reporting Institutions (2012)
OECD, Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions and related guidance
OECD, UNODC and World Bank, Anti-Corruption Ethics and Compliance Handbook for Business (2013)
Wolfsberg Group, Anti-Bribery and Corruption Compliance Programme Guidance (2017)

exposure.rationale: Commission/consultancy payments to agents or shells for foreign official benefit via international wires.

indicators.name: Success fee paid to consultant in a high-corruption market
indicators.canon: Success fee paid to consultant in a high-corruption market
indicators.desc: Large success-based or commission payments to a consultant or agent tied to winning a contract with a state body in a high-corruption-risk jurisdiction.
indicators.ctx: Large success-based or commission payments to a consultant or agent tied to winning a contract with a state body in a high-corruption-risk jurisdiction.
indicators.fp: Genuine commercial agents are commonly paid success fees; rates in some sectors are legitimately high.

indicators.name: Payment to account in third country unrelated to services
indicators.canon: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods
indicators.desc: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
indicators.ctx: Intermediary asks for payment to a bank account in a jurisdiction where neither the service nor the intermediary operates.
indicators.fp: Treasury centralisation or tax-driven structures can place accounts in other countries.

indicators.name: Intermediary shell with no operating footprint
indicators.canon: Shell entity with no operating footprint
indicators.desc: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
indicators.ctx: Consultant is a recently formed company with no website, staff, or track record yet receives large fees from a firm bidding for government work.
indicators.fp: Start-ups and sole-trader specialists may have a limited online presence.

indicators.name: Intermediary linked to a public official or relative
indicators.canon: Intermediary linked to a public official or relative
indicators.desc: Agent or its owners are relatives, associates or former colleagues of an official with influence over the relevant decision.
indicators.ctx: Agent or its owners are relatives, associates or former colleagues of an official with influence over the relevant decision.
indicators.fp: Small markets mean many people have family ties to government; links alone are not wrongdoing.

indicators.name: Vague invoices for unspecified services
indicators.desc: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.
indicators.ctx: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.
indicators.fp: Early-stage or informal advisers may keep thin paperwork.

indicators.name: Gifts, travel or hospitality for officials paid through third parties
indicators.canon: Gifts, travel or hospitality for officials paid through third parties
indicators.desc: Payments for luxury travel, tuition, medical treatment or property for officials or relatives, booked via a vendor or card.
indicators.ctx: Payments for luxury travel, tuition, medical treatment or property for officials or relatives, booked via a vendor or card.
indicators.fp: Official delegations legitimately receive modest hospitality and reasonable travel for site visits.

indicators.name: Payments timed around contract award
indicators.desc: Cluster of payments to an intermediary just before or after a tender decision, licence grant or regulatory approval.
indicators.ctx: Cluster of payments to an intermediary just before or after a tender decision, licence grant or regulatory approval.
indicators.fp: Milestone payments often legitimately align with contract events.

indicators.name: Round-sum payments split below approval limits
indicators.canon: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits
indicators.desc: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.
indicators.ctx: Payments to an intermediary are repeatedly broken into amounts just under internal authorisation thresholds.
indicators.fp: Budget cycles and instalment schedules can create similar patterns.
